Subject: Training opt-out evidence & derivative scope walkthrough

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Healthly's privacy team is ready to move forward but we have a couple of gating asks before procurement will sign off.

Two items on our side:
1) Concrete evidence that requests marked as "no-training" by a customer are excluded from any model improvement or training pipelines across Redwood (including subprocessors). We need an artifacts pack that shows the dataflow and controls.
2) Clarify the scope of "derivative" rights in the DPA: specifically, whether Redwood or any subprocessor can produce derivative models or outputs that would be considered re-usable beyond ephemeral response delivery.

Can you send an evidence pack (subprocessor map + sample logs or manifest) and confirm whether you can provide a DS e-signable addendum for the "no-training" commitment? Ideally we can review before EOD Friday so procurement can prepare PO.

Thanks,
Emma Jones

Vanessa / Team —

We can provide the following as an evidence bundle:
- Subprocessor inventory (latest export) + onboarding dates
- High-level dataflow diagram showing request routing, KV/prefix caching, and storage zones
- Sample evidence_manifest.csv (first/last hashes, retention flags, "no_train" TTL) — see attached stub.
- Ops statement: customer-tagged "no-train" traffic is flagged at the API layer, excluded from telemetry exports and from our model training queues. This also applies to production subprocessors that handle storage (we'll include contractual clauses and subprocessors contact points).

On derivatives: our standard DPA allows delivery of responses to customers and use for service analytics, but we can offer a constrained addendum that prohibits creation of derivative models or reusable model artifacts built from Healthly data. That addendum will be narrow (non-commercialization + no pretraining/finetuning).

Next steps I propose: Legal drafts a two-paragraph operational statement + the addendum redline; Ops assembles the evidence bundle and SFTP instructions; Sales schedules a 30-min walkthrough with Healthly privacy/legal.

I'll attach a sample CSV (evidence_manifest.csv) and a short SFTP how-to (sftp_instructions.txt).

- Dev

--

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks. We can do a short walkthrough and send the evidence pack ahead of time. Proposed times this week: Thu 9:00–9:30 PT or Fri 11:00–11:30 PT. Which works for you?

Attachments I will send once you confirm the meeting: optout_evidence_v1.pdf (operational summary + dataflow), evidence_manifest.csv (sample rows only), and a redline of the no-training addendum (no-train-addendum_redlines.docx).

A couple of clarifying notes on scope so everyone's aligned:
- "No-training" will mean absence from all model pretraining and adaptive finetuning pipelines under Redwood's control and under our contracted subprocessors (we'll include subprocessors by name in the evidence pack).
- "Derivatives" — the addendum will prevent creation of derivative MODEL artifacts intended for re-use outside ephemeral response delivery. It will not prevent Redwood from performing internal, aggregated analytics on telemetry that is completely de-identified and cannot be traced back to Healthly. We'll surface the exact language in the redline.

If that looks correct, pick a meeting time and we'll route a calendar invite + DS link for the addendum.

Best,
Marissa
